title: Component specifications describe styling no stylesheet applies
foundBy: an independent reviewer agent, one of three asked whether each component specification still describes the component that exists
details:
Six specifications document a visual treatment that no rule under `src/styles/` produces. Each was checked against the component's own sheet.

- `components/Table.md:155` promises sortable headers turn `var(--color-accent)` on hover. `src/styles/components/table.css` has one `:hover` rule, at `:233`, and it is for rows.
- `components/Table.md:100` gives the table `background: var(--card)`. `var(--card)` does not appear in `table.css`, so the table takes whatever is behind it.
- `components/StatusBadge.md:60` gives the label `var(--font-weight-medium)`. The label carries `text-label-upper`, which is `var(--font-weight-semibold)` at `src/styles/utilities.css:4`.
- `components/Panel.md:57` pins the title at `11px`. It resolves through `--font-size-label` to 12px, and `DESIGN_SYSTEM_SPEC.md:614` agrees with the code.
- `components/Input.md:98` and `components/SearchInput.md:81` give the placeholder `var(--muted)`. Both sheets use `var(--color-neutral)`, which differs in both themes.
- `components/SplitPane.md:64` describes the hit area as a `::before` extending 2px on each side. `src/styles/components/split-pane.css` has no `::before`, and the real child element is offset to one side instead.

Each of these misleads someone matching their own markup to the library's.
